transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
My wife insisted I come see you, but the real problem is with the hospital. The doctors keep telling me nothing is there, but I know they put something inside me and they’re hiding it.
Can you tell me more about what you think the hospital doctors put inside you and why you believe they're hiding it from you?

Ever since that shoulder scan nine months ago, I'm dead sure they slipped some kind of tracking or testing gadget into me without saying a word. I can actually feel it in there, and I know they're covering it up because they refuse to show me the real records. That's why I've been spending my nights in my workshop building metal rigs to try and catch the signal myself.
Have you experienced any other unusual beliefs or thoughts that you're convinced are true, despite what others might say, such as being followed, plotted against, or having special powers?

No, I don't have any special powers and nobody is physically following me down the street or anything like that. But when it comes to this implant, there is absolutely a plot to keep me quiet. The hospital, the doctors, and probably even the government are actively working together to keep this device a secret and hide the truth from me.
Have you noticed any fluctuations in the intensity of your belief about the implant over the past nine months, or has it remained consistently strong since the shoulder scan?

It hasn't wavered at all, and if anything, I've only become more certain about it over the last nine months. It is incredibly frustrating that everyone keeps denying it when I can feel it right there in my shoulder. The more they try to tell me nothing is there, the more convinced I am that they are hiding the truth.

Have you ever had a period, even briefly, where you questioned the existence of the implant or doubted your belief about the hospital and government conspiracy, or has your conviction remained unwavering since it started?

I have never doubted it for a single second, not even for a moment. Despite my wife and all those doctors trying to tell me I'm crazy, I know what I feel in my shoulder and I've spent months gathering the proof in my workshop. Why would I question it when the physical sensation and their cover-up are so obvious?
Can you tell me if there have been any times when your belief about the implant was not present, or if it has been constant since the shoulder scan nine months ago?

It has been completely constant every single day since that scan nine months ago. There hasn't been a single moment where it wasn't there or where I wasn't thinking about it. It's always present because the device is always in my shoulder.

Have you experienced any other persistent beliefs or fears that you're convinced are true, but others disagree with, outside of the implant and conspiracy, or has your focus been exclusively on this one issue?

No, this is the only issue I'm focused on because it's the only thing they are lying to me about. I don't have any other "theories" or beliefs, but I am absolutely certain about this implant because I can feel it in my shoulder and have spent months trying to prove it. This cover-up is the only thing that matters right now.

You've mentioned that your belief in the implant has been constant since the shoulder scan, but can you tell me if there have been any brief periods where your emotions or behaviors related to this belief have changed, such as feeling more anxious or less anxious about it, or has everything remained consistent?

No, it hasn't gotten any better—if anything, my frustration and anxiety have only grown because nobody will believe me. It just drives me to spend even more time in my shop working on my rigs and researching to find the proof. I've never had a moment where I cared less or felt any less anxious about it.

Can you tell me if there has ever been a time, even a short period, where you felt your belief about the implant might not be true, or has it always been a fixed, unshakeable conviction since it started?

No, I have never doubted it for even a second; it has been a completely firm and unshakeable conviction from the very beginning. Even though my wife and every doctor I see tell me it's not real, I have always felt absolutely certain that the implant is in my shoulder. There has never been a moment where I thought I might be wrong about this.
Can you tell me if you've ever experienced any other delusional beliefs similar to this one before the shoulder scan, or if this is the first time you've had such a strong, unshakeable belief?

No, I have never experienced anything like this before in my life. It only started nine months ago right after that specific shoulder scan, and before that clinic visit, I never had any reason to suspect anyone of doing something like this to me.
